title: jdwp-mcp tool surface
description: The `debug.*` tool surface of one release, published as `tool-surface-<tag>.json` beside the platform binaries (REL-8, #165). It exists so that `what changed for callers between the tag I pin and the one I am moving to` can be answered with two curls and a diff, instead of a clone at two tags. Built by `scripts/tool-surface.py` from the committed snapshots that `cargo test` gates, never regenerated from the binary — an asset re-derived at release time would be a second source of truth beside the files the snapshot tests guard.

$schema.description: This document's stable identifier. Pin it: it is the format, not the release.

kind.description: A discriminator at the document ROOT, so a reader branches on a tag rather than probing for the presence of a field. It exists for the asset this repo does not publish yet: if a second one is ever added, a consumer that already reads this must be able to tell them apart without sniffing.

surface_version.description:
The version of THIS FORMAT, deliberately independent of the crate version. The crate moves for reasons that have nothing to do with the tool surface, so a consumer asking `did the contract change` cannot read the answer off it.

BUMP IT when an existing field here is renamed, removed or changes type, or when a `required` field is added.

DO NOT BUMP IT for an additive OPTIONAL field: an existing consumer sees a byte-identical wire shape on the path it already reads, and a version that moves for changes nobody can observe teaches people to ignore it. Note this is a rule about the SHAPE of this document, not about the tools it describes — a renamed tool changes the surface and not the format, which is what the release notes and `docs/toolkit-contract.md` are for.

release.description: The tag this surface was published for, e.g. `v0.20.0`.

tool_count.description: How many tools are in `tools`. Stated rather than left to be counted, because a consumer diffing two releases wants the headline before the 280KB of prose, and because a producer that silently emitted fewer would otherwise look valid.

argument_count.description: How many arguments across all tools, for the same reason.

tools.description: Every advertised tool, sorted by name.

description.description: THE WORD-WRAPPED FORM, at 110 columns, exactly as `mcp-server/tests/tool-descriptions.txt` holds it — not the raw string the server sends over `tools/list`. Said here rather than left to be assumed. It is the right form for this file's job: the asset exists to be diffed, and wrapping is what makes a corrupted clause a two-line diff instead of a one-character one (DOC-7, #108). The raw string is one `tools/list` call away for anyone who needs it.

schema.description: The generated JSON Schema for this argument, minus its description, exactly as advertised in `inputSchema`. A changed type, default, format, minimum or anyOf arm is visible here.

description.description: Word-wrapped, for the same reason as the tool description above.
